behavior: The .4 publisher stages numeric identity, entity-version, and endpoint values as JSON integers parsed directly into BIGINT fields; the .3 SHA-256 path keeps its prior string staging.
Source, delivery, cursor, property, retained, and other opaque custody values remain strings.

Latest change selection now builds one last-wins dictionary in one pass over the fresh page, then uses expected-O(1) dictionary lookups per touched key instead of repeated reverse scans. This removes that per-entity quadratic scan pattern; it does not establish that the full planner is linear, since other planning and sorting costs remain.

commands: PYTHONPATH=src:tests python -m unittest tests.test_managed_current_xxhash64 tests.test_truss_graph_sql tests.test_whole_graph_sql tests.test_truss_edge_feed tests.test_truss_typed_sql

spark_parser_microcheck.limits: Parses schemas and parameter rows from generated .4 INSERT and MERGE SQL. No Delta writes, graph publication, Unity Catalog, source ACK, resolver, or full-scale qualification.

verification.failed_setup_attempt: Attempt 1 selected system Python 3.9 for the PySpark worker and exited before the parser assertions. Attempt 2 pinned driver and worker Python 3.12 and passed; the first log is retained separately.

test_intent: Exercise min/max signed identities, 2^53+1, create-update-update last-wins delivery/version, create-delete tombstone/history, edge endpoints, exact replay, and opaque custody strings.
Count identity equality comparisons across a distinct-key page to guard against restoring per-key full-page scans without relying on a timing threshold.
qualification: Bounded code-path and Spark JSON parser evidence only. It does not qualify Delta table writes, persisted hash recomputation, physical file pruning, managed Unity Catalog publication, Truss source acceptance, graph-engine execution, or 1B-node/5B-edge scaling.
